title: Foreign Influence Evidence Observatory claim-boundary cases

scope.units: Mixed account, group, source-category, interaction, respondent, and aggregate claims; the unit is explicit in each case.
scope.selection: Prior-known, author-selected hard cases assembled before the immutable preregistration; not a random or held-out sample.
scope.reference_rule: Labels apply only to the exact claim subject and unit on each case, with the stated source and locator.

provenance.review: Single-reviewer provisional labels on all ten cases; independent adjudication pending.
provenance.sources: Four local-source case references cover three report files; six external case references cover five distinct sources. Every case has a source hash, and external source bytes are not redistributed.
provenance.rights: The case-by-case review in BENCHMARK_SOURCE_RIGHTS.json approves the current repository use. Original case metadata is covered by the repository text license; external article bytes and restricted platform or participant data are not redistributed. The three project-authored local report copies do not relicense their underlying datasets or cited works.

evaluation.current_use: Deterministic scorer self-check with safe, targeted-error, and overclaim fixtures.
evaluation.split_rule_for_future_evaluation: Hold out entire campaign or source dataset and collection-period blocks; never split rows from the same group across train and test.

risks: Selection favors illustrative claim-boundary failures and cannot estimate their prevalence.
Most claim slots are unknown; abstention and supported-claim coverage must accompany unsupported-assertion rates.
The one contradicted automation case is a group-level universal assertion, not an account-level reference-negative sample.
Historical detector versions, platforms, and periods cannot be assumed to represent current deployment.
Independent label adjudication and source-license review are incomplete.
prohibited_uses: Do not report the scorer fixtures as performance of a real detector or language model.
Do not describe the contradicted-claim assertion rate as a population false-positive rate or false discovery proportion.
Do not turn unknown cases into verified negatives or publish account-level accusations from them.
Do not claim a final benchmark release until the preregistered gates pass.
